claim.quote: A search for disappearance of antineutrinos to a sterile state has been conducted using complementary model-dependent frequentist and Bayesian fits, providing constraints on the allowed region of the Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; the paper was later published in Phys. Rev. D (not independently checked here).

key_value_text.quote: A total of 29479 $\pm$ 603 (stat.) antineutrino candidates have been selected, corresponding to an average rate of 105 events per day and a signal-to-background ratio of 0.27.
key_value_text.value: 29479 +- 603 (stat.) antineutrino candidates, 105 events/day, signal-to-background 0.27, in 280 reactor-on days

name: Search for Very-Short-Baseline Oscillations of Reactor Antineutrinos with the SoLid Detector

summary.plain: SoLid reported its first scientific result: with 280 days of reactor-on data it selected about 29,500 antineutrino candidates and searched for their disappearance into a sterile type, constraining the region allowed by the reactor antineutrino anomaly.
summary.technical: 280 reactor-on days (55 MW mean power) and 172 reactor-off days; 29,479 +- 603 (stat.) candidates (105/day, S/B 0.27); model-dependent frequentist and Bayesian disappearance fits constrain the RAA allowed region.

title: Search for Very-Short-Baseline Oscillations of Reactor Antineutrinos with the SoLid Detector
why_it_matters: The first physics result from a very-short-baseline experiment using a highly granular 6Li/PVT detector at a highly enriched uranium reactor.
